A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe CHEEMS and contain matching main sections and Appendices A–G. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model evaluations, dataset ablations, downstream correlations, scaling experiments, and annotation analyses, including Tables 2–5 and Figures 5–7 and 15.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including CheemsRM evaluations, dataset-construction experiments, and the appendix conflict-rate and annotation-bias analyses.

M1.justification: The graph-based conflict resolution, human-supervised filtering of GPT annotations, length debiasing, batch construction, and regularized reward-model loss remain unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CheemsBench subsets, CheemsPreference and comparison training datasets, RewardBench, and downstream Human Win-rate, MT-bench-zh, and MT-bench tasks. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in Tables 2–4 and 8 and Figure 5. This includes the same discriminative and generative RMs, alternative preference datasets, and RewardBench/RMB benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: Accuracy/exact-match scoring, category averaging, response sampling, Best-of-32 evaluation, the 87-instruction Human Win-rate sample, and the 26-RM correlation assessment are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same training settings.

E4.justification: Both retain identical category and downstream-correlation analyses, dataset-construction ablations, data/model scaling studies, and appendix conflict-rate and annotation-bias analyses (Figures 4–7 and 15; Tables 4–5).

E5.justification: Appendix F explicitly reports a single experimental run in both versions. Point-estimate reporting remains unchanged, with no added repeated-seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Tables 2 and 4 retain CheemsRM's 0.657 CheemsBench overall score and 0.919 RewardBench score; the appendix conflict ratios and full baseline results also match.

T1.justification: The accuracy/exact-match definitions and Bradley–Terry and regularization equations (1–4) are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same mathematical reasoning about preference graphs and partial rankings.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark and preference-dataset contributions, state-of-the-art performance claim, and claims about the importance of human supervision.

C2.justification: Interpretations of annotation quality, human-instruction difficulty, debiasing, and scaling remain unchanged. The limitations and ethical discussion retain the same qualifications concerning cultural coverage, annotator subjectivity, and generalization beyond Chinese and English.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code and data availability statement pointing to AlignRM/CheemsRM at the end of Section 1; v1 lacks this access pointer. Existing implementation details, annotation instructions, and hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography retain the same cited works and positioning relative to existing reward-model research. No substantive related-work discussion or novelty argument changes.

P1.justification: v3 corrects affiliation indices, identifies corresponding authors, and adds a short resource-availability statement and an Acknowledgment section. These are limited editorial additions; the scientific prose and logical section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 removes printed page-number footers and changes some placements: Figure 9 moves from PDF page 14 to 15, and Table 9 moves to the right column on PDF page 19. Figure and table content, captions, and graphical designs are retained.

improvement.justification: The new Section 1 code/data pointer improves resource discoverability, and corrected author and affiliation information improves documentation accuracy. Scientific methods, results, analyses, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited to access information and editorial quality.
